extraction.name: VQAonline
extraction.description: A fully authentic visual question answering dataset containing 64,696 examples sourced from Stack Exchange online communities. Each example includes a natural language question, supplementary context, an image, and an answer accepted by the question asker. The dataset covers 105 topics across five super-categories and has answers averaging 173 words.
extraction.license: CC BY-SA 4.0; the authors state that they adhered to Stack Exchange's data license restrictions.
extraction.creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, and Danna Gurari
extraction.inLanguage: Multilingual; most visual questions are written in English.
extraction.citeAs: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, and Danna Gurari. Fully Authentic Visual Question Answering Dataset from Online Communities. arXiv:2311.15562v4 [cs.CV], 17 July 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors scraped publicly available Stack Exchange data spanning August 2010 to November 2022. They collected examples containing a question, context, an image, and at least one answer, retaining only those with an answer marked as accepted by the question asker. Questions originated from post titles, context from post bodies, and images from URL links supplied by users. Answers were publicly contributed by other users. Data came from 105 topical sites across culture and recreation, life and arts, science, professional, and business super-categories. Filtering reduced 330,705 candidate visual questions to 64,696 examples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, User-generated content data, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Examples without an accepted answer were removed, reducing 330,705 candidates to 165,766. Examples whose images could not be downloaded from the provided links were also removed, reducing 65,849 examples to the final 64,696.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Stack Exchange user-generated questions, context, image links, answers, accepted-answer selections, and voting scores. The Stack Exchange archive is hosted at https://archive.org/details/stackexchange in XML format.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: August 2010 to November 2022 is the coverage period of the source data; the dates when scraping was performed are not stated.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All images were converted to PNG for format consistency. Training, validation, and test splits contain 665, 285, and 63,746 examples respectively. For topics with at least 20 examples, seven examples were randomly selected for training and three for validation. No topics were excluded from the test dataset.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors excluded 75 technology topics because their questions typically concerned language problems such as code in screenshots. They retained examples with questions, context, images, and accepted answers. They removed examples with question or accepted-answer scores of zero or less, multiple images including GIFs, visual answers, or images that could not be downloaded. The filtering sequence reduced 330,705 candidates to 165,766 after requiring accepted answers, 119,177 after score filtering, 85,573 after removing multiple-image questions, 65,849 after removing visual answers, and 64,696 after excluding failed image downloads.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Reference answers were authored by Stack Exchange users and marked as accepted by the original question askers. Topic labels originated from users posting within topic-specific communities. For dataset characterization, the authors manually labeled sampled images for screenshots, infographics, question alignment, context alignment, and image necessity. User-intention annotations covered 105 VQAs, one per topic, using eight categories: advice, evidence, identification, instruction, opinion, reason, verification, and other. Crowdworkers received definitions, two examples per category, individual Zoom training, and a qualifying test. Two independent workers labeled each item, with a third worker resolving disagreements. In a separate IRB-approved model-evaluation study, ten domain experts each assessed 20 VQAs in their specialty and rated six model answers per VQA as incorrect (0), partially correct (0.5), or correct (1), yielding 1,200 judgments for 200 VQAs. Correctness could be established either by agreement with reference-answer key points or by the expert's independent judgment.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk was used to recruit user-intention crowdworkers, who recorded labels in a provided spreadsheet and received training through Zoom. Domain experts used a home-grown web-based annotation interface and recorded results in spreadsheets. Code for the interface is available at https://github.com/VQAonline/VQAonlineVisualization.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Two author annotators refined the user-intention taxonomy through four rounds of labeling and disagreement resolution on 105 visual questions. Agreement accuracy increased from 53.3% to 87.5%, and Cohen's kappa increased from 45.24% to 84.69%. For crowdworker intention labels, 25 of 105 initial pairs disagreed; a third worker selected between the two proposed labels. A supplementary table separately describes final labels as majority votes from three crowdsourced labels per VQA. For domain-expert evaluations, the authors provided individual training, offered ongoing clarification, and inspected annotation time as a quality-control proxy. They compared aggregated human ratings with automatic evaluation metrics using Pearson and Spearman correlations.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each dataset example has one retained accepted reference answer. For the 105-item user-intention study, two independent human labels were collected per item, with a third label for the 25 disagreements; a supplementary table instead describes three labels per item with majority voting. For model evaluation, one domain expert rated each of six model answers per VQA, producing six judgments per VQA across 200 VQAs.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: User-intention crowdworkers were located in the United States, had completed more than 500 Mechanical Turk HITs, and had approval ratings above 95%. Ten domain-expert evaluators were located in the United States and each held at least a Master's degree in a field related to the assigned topic. Their specialties were Physical Fitness, Botany, Music, Mechanics, Politics, Law, Chinese Language, Economics, Statistics, and Artificial Intelligence. Two paper authors participated in taxonomy-development annotation.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5 was prompted with questions and context to bootstrap an initial user-intention taxonomy. DeepSolo detected text in all dataset images, and text-presence metadata was publicly shared. LLaMA2 was used as an automated evaluation metric to rate model-generated answers against reference answers as totally wrong (0), partially correct (0.5), or totally correct (1).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors anticipate that improved models developed using VQAonline could benefit community question-answering platforms, children's learning-assistance tools, virtual assistants, visual dialogue and query, and visual search and browsing. They argue that understanding user intention could support human-centered VQA systems with answers better tailored to user needs. They also highlight potential underrepresentation of people in poverty-stricken areas and geographic imbalance among Stack Exchange users.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas because contributors have access to mobile devices and the Internet. The paper describes geographic representation as unbalanced, with more users from the US, India, and Europe and fewer from places such as Egypt. Topics have a long-tail distribution: 52% of all VQAs belong to the 24 science topics, representing about 23% of topics. Image samples show a high prevalence of screenshots, reflecting users' tendency to ask questions about the digital realm.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to selected Stack Exchange communities and excludes technology topics, questions without accepted answers, non-positive-score questions or answers, multiple-image questions, visual answers, and unavailable images. Standard short-answer VQA evaluation metrics are ill-suited to its lengthy answers. In a manually analyzed sample, only 65.7% of images were necessary for answering the question. Benchmark contamination is a concern because several evaluated models were confirmed or suspected to have trained on Stack Exchange data and may have encountered dataset examples. The ten topics used for expert evaluation might not represent the full dataset. The authors also acknowledge socioeconomic and geographic representation limitations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, Testing. The provided splits support few-shot learning, and the paper benchmarks vision-language models in zero-shot and one-shot settings. Additional uses include studying long-form VQA evaluation, user intentions, multilingual and text-based VQA, domain-specific knowledge, image understanding, reasoning, and hallucinations in authentic use cases. The authors evaluate lengthy answers using long-form text and image-compatibility metrics rather than standard short-answer VQA metrics.
